notice: Jarvis's curated guide to the console screens. Every workspace/view pair from ConsoleContext has an entry in both languages; every spotlight is a data-guide anchor in the markup.

overview/fund.title: Overview → Fund
overview/fund.what: The state of the whole well stock at the selected step: how many wells operate, how much is produced and injected, what the compensation is and how much NPV has accumulated.
overview/fund.how_to_read: Each tile is one value and its run across steps. Compensation is read against its corridor: going above threatens rising pressure and an opened fracture, going below means falling pressure and lost production. Strictly, compensation is computed in reservoir conditions through the PVT formation volume factors, not as a surface ratio of injection to offtake. The trust board below names the source of every artifact.
questions: How is the field doing now?

field/projection.title: Field → Projection
field/projection.what: A map of the well stock: wells at their deck coordinates and the measured links between injectors and producers.
field/projection.how_to_read: A node is a well, its colour set by the chosen layer: role, water cut or rate. An edge is the measured influence of injection on production; the thicker it is, the stronger. The λ on an edge is measured by a design of experiments over perturbed runs, not derived from distance: nearby wells may well be unconnected. The λ threshold slider cuts off weak links so that the significant ones show through 2375 edges. Barriers are equilibration region boundaries, pinch-outs and bands of inactive cells; an edge crossing a barrier is drawn dashed and needs verification.
questions: Whom does this well's injection influence?
What is a barrier and are there faults?

field/maps.title: Field → Maps
field/maps.what: Maps of reservoir properties by layer from the Model_Z deck: porosity, permeability, net-to-gross, zones and equilibrium regions, top depth and the active-cell mask. Wells are drawn over the map on the same projection as on Projection.
field/maps.how_to_read: Every grid cell is coloured by the value of the chosen property; the scale is linear, logarithmic for permeability and categorical for zones and regions. These are static properties of the model, not a calculation: the dynamics come from the well layer that lives on the player's steps — the fill shows whether a well is open or shut, the marker colour is the bottomhole pressure and the ring is the water cut. The provenance plate says plainly: Model_Z deck, statics.
questions: Where is porosity highest on the map?
How does layer 1 differ from layer 2?
Which layer does this well sit in?
What do the FIP zones show?

history/matrix.title: History → Matrix
history/matrix.what: The field's whole history on one canvas: wells vertically, control steps horizontally, and events — commissionings, conversions and shut-ins — as marks at the intersections.
history/matrix.how_to_read: A column is one month of the horizon, a row is one well. A mark means a state change at exactly that step; the year ticks on the axis help hit the right year.
questions: What happened to the field in 2015?
When was it converted to injection?

history/wall.title: History → Wall
history/wall.what: Each well's life as its own band: how long it worked, when it was shut in and in what role it lived.
history/wall.how_to_read: A band reads left to right as time. A gap is a shut-in, a change of fill is a change of role. This shows which wells carried the field through the whole horizon and which entered late.
questions: How long did this well operate?
Which was shut in most often?

history/table.title: History → Table
history/table.what: The numbers as they are: for each well at the selected step — setpoint and fact, liquid rate, injection, water cut and bottomhole pressure.
history/table.how_to_read: Columns sort on a header click. A dash means the value is undefined in the data, not zero: substituting zeros here is forbidden.

decisions/council.title: Decisions → Council
decisions/council.what: How a limited resource is allocated: available water is split across areas and, within an area, across wells.
decisions/council.how_to_read: The area level with its limits is on top, the well level with assigned setpoints below. The wells' sum does not exceed the area limit, and the areas' sum does not exceed available water.
questions: How much water did this area get?

decisions/rules.title: Decisions → Rules
decisions/rules.what: Rules R0 to R7: the statement of each, when it fired and with what actual inputs.
decisions/rules.how_to_read: A row is a rule. Expanding it shows the Trace records: step, well, inputs and the decision taken. A rule without a measured contribution is marked unmeasured, not zero.
questions: Why was this well shut in?

money/rank.title: Money → NPV rank
money/rank.what: Who earned what: the final NPV broken down by well, and the measured contribution of each rule.
money/rank.how_to_read: Wells are sorted by contribution — those pulling the total up at the top, those in the red at the bottom. Below is the ablation table: how much NPV drops if a rule is switched off.

money/comparison.title: Money → Scenario comparison
money/comparison.what: Scenarios side by side: each one's NPV, verification status, OOD score and worst regret across the battery.
money/comparison.how_to_read: It only makes sense to compare the NPV of verified scenarios: a surrogate prediction and a verified run are different values and are labelled differently. A high OOD means the prediction cannot be trusted.

money/constraints.title: Money → Constraints
money/constraints.what: The scenario's external bounds: injection and liquid limits, production floors, water-cut ceilings, well outages and infrastructure.
money/constraints.how_to_read: An empty constraint set means an unconstrained scenario, not missing data. Outages are given as an interval of steps and cannot be overridden by policy decisions.
questions: What constraints does this scenario have?
What is the volume n of additional water?

header.title: Console header
header.what: The shared context: the chosen scenario, the current step date, language and theme.
header.how_to_read: Everything shown below in the console refers to exactly this scenario and this step. Changing the scenario in the header redraws every screen.
questions: How do I change the language?

player.title: Step player
player.what: Scrubbing the horizon by control steps: 225 control dates from 2007 to the end of the horizon.
player.how_to_read: The player position sets the step for every screen at once. Marks on the track are steps where field events occurred.
questions: How do I jump to January 2015?
What was at the previous step?

inspector.title: Well inspector
inspector.what: The selected well's card: role, status, setpoint and fact, water cut, bottomhole pressure and its contribution to NPV.
inspector.how_to_read: The inspector always shows the well at the player's current step. A dash means the value is undefined in the data, not zero.
questions: What is its contribution to NPV?

command-palette.title: Command palette
command-palette.what: A fast jump between screens and to wells by name, without the mouse.
command-palette.how_to_read: It opens on a shortcut and searches screen names and well numbers; picking from the list moves the console there at once.
questions: How do I switch screens quickly?
How do I find a well by number?
